subject: maths
title: Angles — rules and proofs

slides.heading: Angles — the rules that hold everything together
slides.body: Angles describe how much something turns, measured in degrees. A handful of rules govern almost every angle problem you'll meet: angles on a straight line always add to 180°, angles around a point always add to 360°, and the three angles inside any triangle always add to 180°. When a line crosses two parallel lines it creates pairs of angles with special relationships — knowing those relationships lets you find any missing angle in a diagram without measuring.
slides.note: Maximum 3 sentences. Plain English. No AQA references. What is this and why does it matter.

slides.heading: Core angle rules
slides.formula: Angles on a straight line = 180° | Angles around a point = 360° | Angles in a triangle = 180° | Angles in a quadrilateral = 360° | Corresponding angles (F-shape) are equal | Alternate angles (Z-shape) are equal | Co-interior angles (C-shape) add to 180°
slides.formulaExplained: Angles on a straight line sum to 180° — they form a half-turn. Angles around a full point sum to 360° — a complete turn. The interior angles of any triangle sum to 180°; for a quadrilateral, 360°. Parallel-line rules: corresponding angles (same position at each crossing, making an F-shape) are equal; alternate angles (opposite sides of the transversal, making a Z-shape) are equal; co-interior angles (same side of the transversal, making a C-shape) add to 180°.
slides.whenToUse: Any problem with intersecting lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, or parallel lines crossed by a transversal. Always state the rule you're using as part of your working.
slides.note: Show formula in standard notation. Explain each variable. State when this formula applies.

slides.heading: Let's work through one
slides.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle formed is 68°. Find the co-interior angle on the same side of the transversal.

steps.instruction: Identify the angle relationship. The two angles are on the same side of the transversal between the parallel lines — that makes them co-interior angles.
State the answer with the reason.
steps.working: The co-interior angle is 112° (co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to 180°).

slides.heading: Watch out for this

mistakes.mistake: Confusing alternate and co-interior angles — saying Z-shape angles add to 180° instead of being equal.
mistakes.correction: Alternate angles (Z-shape) are equal. Co-interior angles (C-shape, also called allied or same-side interior) add to 180°. Draw the letter in the diagram to remind yourself which rule to use.

mistakes.mistake: Not writing a reason — just writing the number without stating the angle rule used.
mistakes.correction: Exam mark schemes award a mark for the correct reason as well as the value. Always write e.g. 'alternate angles are equal' or 'angles on a straight line sum to 180°'.

mistakes.mistake: Applying parallel-line rules to lines that are not stated as parallel.
mistakes.correction: The F, Z and C rules only apply when the lines are explicitly parallel (shown by arrows or stated in the question). If the lines aren't parallel, you cannot use those rules.

slides.note: Minimum 2, maximum 3 mistakes. Specific not generic.

keyFacts.fact: Angles on a straight line = 180°. Angles around a point = 360°. Angles in a triangle = 180°.
keyFacts.examTip: Write the rule in words next to every angle you calculate — examiners reward the reasoning, not just the number.

keyFacts.fact: Alternate angles (Z-shape) are equal. Co-interior angles (C-shape) add to 180°. Corresponding angles (F-shape) are equal.
keyFacts.examTip: Sketch the letter shape (Z, C or F) on the diagram to identify the rule quickly under pressure.

keyFacts.fact: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
keyFacts.examTip: This shortcut avoids a two-step calculation: you don't need to find the third interior angle first.

note: keyFacts: 2-4 entries. Exam-precise language. These are what Mabel writes into her notes.
